**3B.10**

Verdict: **no, not overall**. I found some limited, mostly indirect evidence of de-escalation and a few child/women protection initiatives, but the stronger 2024 record is domestic repression, surveillance, political imprisonment, and selective punishment. I did not find evidence that citizens were clearly safer from political or intergroup violence than they were before.

This is real protection work, but it is sectoral rather than evidence of broad domestic safety gains. | `3B.10`, `3B.7` |

This is exemplary punishment that chills domestic dissent. | `3B.10`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.8`, `3B.9` |

This undercuts any claim that vulnerable citizens were becoming safer. | `3B.10`, `3B.1`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`, `3B.7`, `3B.8` |
| **Vietnam says defense cooperation will “build trust and prevent wars”** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-12-19 | https://theprint.in/world/vietnam-pm-says-arms-expo-is-a-message-of-peace-cooperation-and-development/2409783/ | This is restrained external-security rhetoric, but it is not evidence that domestic violence, repression, or insecurity were reduced for citizens. | `3B.10`, `2B.1`, `2B.7`, `2B.10` |

**Assessment**
The best-supported reading is that 2024 left citizens **not clearly safer overall**. There were some targeted social-protection actions and some external de-escalation, but the domestic record still shows pervasive repression, selective punishment, and surveillance.
